summary: U.S. equity futures slumped Monday morning as Middle East tensions reignited following weekend U.S. strikes on Iranian rocket launchers near the Strait of Hormuz, sending oil prices surging over 2%. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole speech on Friday continues to weigh on sentiment, with the two-year Treasury yield jumping over 10 basis points as traders increased bets on a September rate hike. The S&P 500 fell 0.3% Friday to close at 7,711.76, while the Dow dropped 464 points, snapping a five-day win streak. Bitcoin pulled back from last week's rally above $80,000, trading near $77,000 after strong ETF inflows earlier in the week confirmed institutional demand. Chicago PMI data collapsed to 47.1 in August from 57.6 in July, missing estimates badly and adding to growth concerns as markets close out the month with limited earnings catalysts this week.

signals.title: Fed Chair Warsh delivers hawkish Jackson Hole speech, fueling rate-hike bets
signals.desc: Kevin Warsh's hawkish remarks on Friday drove Treasury yields higher and increased market expectations for a September rate hike, pressuring equities into the weekend.

signals.title: U.S. strikes Iranian targets near Strait of Hormuz, oil surges 2%
signals.desc: U.S. military action against Iranian rocket launchers preparing to mine the Strait of Hormuz escalated Middle East tensions, sending crude prices sharply higher and weighing on equity futures.

signals.title: Chicago PMI collapses to 47.1, far below consensus of 58
signals.desc: Manufacturing activity in the Chicago region contracted sharply in August, falling from 57.6 to 47.1 and missing estimates by a wide margin, signaling deteriorating growth momentum.

signals.title: Bitcoin pulls back to $77,000 after topping $81,000 last week
signals.desc: Bitcoin consolidated gains after briefly surging past $80,000 mid-week on strong ETF inflows; institutional demand remains intact despite the pullback from recent highs.

signals.title: Tech sector outperforms as Nvidia holds gains post-earnings
signals.desc: Information Technology Select Sector rose 3.2% Friday, the only S&P sector in positive territory, with Nvidia edging higher as last week's blowout earnings continue to support chip stocks.

verdict: Risk-off tone dominates as geopolitical flare-ups and hawkish Fed messaging overshadow tech strength; expect choppy Monday session with defensive positioning into September data.
